analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md changes one table region (head lines ~1968-1971). It updates the reconnect-policy constants: backoff moves to CoordinatorReconnectPolicy, resets after a 60 s stable session counted from the register frame, and waits a random 0-1 s after close code 1012. The ping and pong row is unchanged apart from its source reference. The two supplied units are head-text excerpts from earlier in the same file (lines 805-1727). They are surrounding context, not the changed lines, and the changed lines themselves (~1968) are not visible in either unit. I examined that context against TB-002, T-010, T-041, T-053 and TB-012. It describes Autopilot consent, drain/stop/restart, the addon hold CLI, doctor/status diagnostics, benchmark flags, logout and unenroll guidance, and report upload. None of this adds code, endpoints, defaults or controls; it is prose. The prefix-cache status text (prefix_cache=, key_unavailable) is consistent with the retained T-041 posture and exposes no new data. The report section states that device-wide logs are scrubbed and that automatic upload is disabled. The addon docs describe an owner-only lifecycle mailbox and a refusal of release without --force while the machine lock is held, consistent with TB-012/T-059.

The shorter reconnect delay after 1012 (0-1 s random) and the backoff reset after a stable 60 s session are described only in docs. The actual reconnect policy (CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify the code against the docs. Any reconnect storm or thundering-herd availability concern, or a bypass of re-registration and re-attestation (T-053 stale authorization surviving a connection change), would need review of the source change in the companion PR. Recorded as an unverified contract, not a finding.
